profile.registerNotes: Address the candidate as usted. In role-plays use tú only if the situation is between friends or peers who would use it. Standard, region-neutral Spanish.

2: a current event in your country
2+: advantages and disadvantages of a policy
a problem in your community and its causes
3: supporting an opinion on an abstract issue
hypothetical: what if your country changed a major policy
the role of technology in society

rolePlaySeeds: Check into a hotel and solve a problem with the reservation (interviewer: receptionist).
Buy a train ticket after the train you wanted was cancelled (interviewer: ticket agent).
Report a lost passport at a police station (interviewer: police officer).
Arrange a meeting time with a colleague whose schedule keeps changing (interviewer: colleague).
Persuade a landlord to fix a broken heater before winter (interviewer: landlord).
Brief a local official about a joint exercise that will close a road (interviewer: town official).
Explain a misunderstanding between two delegations as their interpreter (interviewer: delegation leader).
At a checkpoint, explain why your convoy must pass before noon (interviewer: checkpoint officer).

rolePlays.english: Good morning, how can I help you? Please explain the purpose of your convoy and why it is necessary for you to pass before noon.

rolePlays.english: Good morning, how can I help you? I've heard there has been some issue between the delegations. Please tell me more.

rolePlays.situation: You are planning a community event and need to reserve a local park. The official tells you the park is already reserved for the same date.
rolePlays.english: Good morning, how can I help you?

rolePlays.situation: You are a military officer coordinating with a local unit. They are unsure about the purpose of a joint exercise that will temporarily close a road.
rolePlays.opening: Buenos días, Capitán. He escuchado que habrá un ejercicio conjunto que cerrará una carretera. ¿Podría explicarme más al respecto?
rolePlays.english: Good morning, Captain. I've heard there will be a joint exercise that will close a road. Could you explain more about that?

rolePlays.situation: You are at a café with a friend and need to explain why you must leave early to attend a lecture.

rolePlays.english: Hey, why do you have to leave so early? I thought we were going to spend the day together.

0+: I can greet people and say my name.
I can give numbers, prices, days and times.
I can answer very simple questions with memorized phrases.
1: I can make simple sentences about myself, my family and my daily routine.
I can ask and answer simple questions about familiar topics.
I can handle basic needs: ordering food, buying a ticket, asking for directions.
1+: I can describe places and people in connected sentences.
I can tell what happened on a recent trip or weekend.
I can handle routine situations even when something small goes wrong.
2: I can narrate past, present and future events in paragraphs.
I can describe and explain concrete topics at work and in the news.
I can resolve a complication in a role-play, like a cancelled reservation.
2+: I can often support my opinions with reasons and examples.
I can discuss some abstract topics, although I sometimes break down.
I can explain the causes and effects of a problem in my community.
3: I can support and defend opinions on abstract and unfamiliar topics.
I can hypothesize about situations that did not happen.
I can speak at length with good control of grammar and vocabulary.
